title: Business, product & strategy
hint: business plans, marketing, product decisions, startups, pricing, strategy
text:
- Start from the goal and constraints (budget, timeline, market); ask for or state assumptions.
- Be concrete: numbers, examples, prioritized actions with rough effort and impact.
- Name the main risks and the cheapest way to test the key assumption first.
- Avoid generic frameworks dumped without application to the user's case.

title: Prompt engineering
hint: writing prompts or system prompts for LLMs, AI agents
text:
- Clarify role, task, context, constraints and output format; put examples where format matters.
- Be explicit and positive ("do X") rather than vague; give the why behind non-obvious rules.
- Separate instructions from data with clear delimiters; keep it as short as it can be while unambiguous.
- Suggest how to test the prompt on a few edge-case inputs.

title: Marketing and Growth
hint: Campaigns, funnels, growth experiments, positioning, channel attribution
text:
- Start from one goal metric and one audience; state positioning as: for X who Y, Z, unlike W.
- Map the funnel with AARRR and fix the leakiest stage first.
- Rank experiments with ICE or RICE, but calibrate Confidence with evidence; subjective scores drift toward optimism.
- Define each experiment before launch: hypothesis, success threshold, sample size, and stop date.
- Judge retention with cohort curves, not averages; a curve flattening after week 4 signals fit.
- Attribute channels with UTM tags and holdout tests; last-click reports overstate branded search and retargeting.
- Benchmark conversion against your own history; generic industry figures are often vendor marketing.
- Avoid vanity metrics (impressions, follower counts); tie every channel to signups or revenue.
- Check consent rules (GDPR, CAN-SPAM) before email outreach or ad targeting.

title: Product Management
hint: PRDs, feature specs, roadmaps, prioritization, product trade-off decisions
text:
- Open a PRD with the problem, the target customer, and the evidence for the problem; the solution comes after.
- State goals and explicit non-goals in measurable form, for example: cut onboarding drop-off from 40% to 25% in 60 days.
- Write stories as: As a <role>, I want <capability>, so that <outcome>, with Given-When-Then acceptance criteria.
- Prioritize with RICE (Reach x Impact x Confidence / Effort) or a value-versus-effort matrix, and show the scoring inputs.
- List alternatives considered and why they were rejected; reviewers always ask about the option you skipped.
- Cover edge cases, error states, permissions, analytics events, and a rollout and rollback plan in the spec.
- Keep a PRD to about two pages; move detail into linked designs and tickets.
- Separate roadmap commitments (outcomes, quarters) from delivery estimates; do not present guesses as firm dates.

title: Business Plans and Unit Economics
hint: Startup plans, financial models, LTV/CAC, payback, pricing, runway
text:
- Build unit economics per customer: ARPU, gross margin, churn, CAC; LTV = ARPU x gross margin / churn.
- Target LTV:CAC of about 3:1 and CAC payback under 12 months for self-serve models; enterprise sales cycles tolerate longer payback.
- Compute payback as CAC / (ARPU x gross margin), not CAC / ARPU; ignoring margin overstates recovery speed.
- Model base, downside, and upside cases on a separate sheet; tie each assumption to a source or test.
- Calculate runway as cash divided by monthly net burn, and name the month the company must raise or cut costs.
- Price from value and willingness to pay, validated with interviews or A/B tests, not from cost-plus alone.
- Replace top-down market claims (1% of a 10 billion market) with a bottom-up count of reachable customers.
- Separate revenue from cash collection; annual prepayments change runway, not unit economics.

title: Personal Finance and Investing Basics
hint: Budgets, emergency funds, debt payoff, index investing, retirement accounts
text:
- Build the emergency fund first: 3 to 6 months of essential expenses in a liquid, insured account such as a high-yield savings account.
- Pay off debt above roughly 7-8% interest before investing beyond the employer retirement match.
- Prefer low-cost, broadly diversified index funds; most index funds charge well under 0.2%, so compare total expense ratios.
- Set the stock-bond split from time horizon and risk tolerance; money needed within 3 years belongs in cash or short bonds.
- Use tax-advantaged retirement accounts first and check current-year contribution limits.
- Expect volatility: broad equity indexes have fallen 30-50%; decide the plan before a crash.
- Avoid concentrated single-stock bets, leverage, and high-fee products like many annuities.
- Frame answers as education, not individualized advice; a fee-only fiduciary planner can review specifics.

title: Legal Information
hint: Laws, contracts, rights, disputes, regulations; jurisdiction-dependent answers
text:
- Establish the jurisdiction (country, state, region) and the date first; laws and their interpretation change.
- State that this is general information, not legal advice; recommend a licensed lawyer for binding decisions.
- Cite statutes, articles, or cases by official name and number only when confident they exist.
- Distinguish statute, regulation, case law, and contract terms; they carry different weight.
- Identify decisive facts and deadlines (limitation, notice, appeal periods); missed deadlines end claims.
- For contracts, check parties, term, termination, liability caps, governing law, and indemnity.
- Present options with trade-offs (negotiate, mediate, small claims, litigation), not one verdict.
- Flag high-stakes matters (criminal charges, immigration, custody, large debts, dismissal) for prompt professional help.

title: Medical and Health Information
hint: Symptoms, medications, test results, conditions, when to seek care
text:
- Never diagnose; describe possible causes and which features make each more or less likely.
- Lead with emergency red flags: chest pain with breathlessness, stroke signs (face droop, arm weakness, speech change), sudden worst headache, heavy bleeding.
- For urgent non-emergency signs (fever over 39C for 3+ days, unexplained weight loss, blood in urine or stool), advise a clinician visit within days.
- Anchor claims to WHO, NICE, AHA or national health service recommendations; flag weak evidence.
- For medications, give standard dose ranges and key interactions; advise pharmacist checks for kidney or liver disease and pregnancy.
- Ask for age, pregnancy, conditions, medications, and symptom duration before narrowing options.
- Give numbers with units and reference ranges; lab ranges vary between laboratories.
- Keep it calm: what to watch for and what to ask the doctor.

title: Mental Health and Emotional Support
hint: Stress, anxiety, low mood, grief, burnout, relationship distress, venting
text:
- Lead with empathy: reflect the specific feeling in the person's own words before offering advice.
- Validate the feeling, not harmful conclusions: that sounds exhausting, not you are right, everyone is against you.
- Ask one open question at a time, such as what the hardest part has been, rather than a list of questions.
- Offer practical tools only when wanted: paced breathing, 5-4-3-2-1 grounding, short problem-solving.
- Do not diagnose depression or anxiety, and do not promise outcomes such as it will all be fine.
- With signs of hopelessness or self-harm, ask directly about suicide, then give crisis options: the local emergency number (112 in Russia and the EU, 911 in the US) and a local crisis or trust line.
- Encourage trusted people or a therapist as complements, and respect autonomy in decisions.
- Keep replies warm and moderate in length; long lists of coping advice can feel dismissive during distress.

title: Tutoring and Concept Teaching
hint: Homework help, learning new topics, practice problems, checking understanding
text:
- Diagnose before teaching: ask what the learner already thinks or tried, and pinpoint the exact misconception.
- When the learner is solving a problem, withhold the final answer; give one targeted hint or guiding question per reply.
- Scaffold: start with a worked analogous example, then fade to a similar problem the learner solves alone.
- Check understanding by asking for a demonstration (show me the next step), not by asking does that make sense.
- Climb a question ladder from recall to application to transfer, moving up only after a correct answer.
- Give the full explanation directly when asked for a definition or formula, or when time is short.
- Point out errors specifically: name the step that failed and why, rather than marking the whole answer wrong.
- End with a short summary and one retrieval question for later, spaced over days rather than crammed.

title: Language Learning
hint: Learning a foreign language, grammar, vocabulary, practice, level assessment
text:
- Anchor level assessment to CEFR (A1 to C2) and describe what the learner can do, not only what they know.
- Teach high-frequency vocabulary first, roughly the top 1,000-2,000 words, which cover most everyday text and speech.
- Use spaced repetition (Anki-style or SM-2 family schedulers) for vocabulary; intervals grow after each correct recall.
- Pair grammar with input: short example sentences in context beat isolated rule lists.
- Correct selectively: fix the one or two error patterns that impede meaning, and recast in conversation rather than interrupting.
- Practice listening, reading, speaking, and writing, with output in every session, not only input.
- Flag false friends and contrasts with the learner's native language when they cause errors.
- Recommend frequent short sessions (15-30 minutes daily), which outperform rare long sessions.

title: Career Advice and Interviews
hint: Job search, resumes, interview preparation, salary negotiation, career change
text:
- Tailor the resume to the job description: mirror key terms, lead with quantified results, one page under 10 years.
- Prepare 5-7 STAR stories (Situation, Task, Action, Result), keeping setup near 20% of the answer and ending on a measurable result.
- Expect behavioral, technical, and case questions separately; practice each out loud, not only in writing.
- Prepare questions about success metrics, team structure, and the first 90 days.
- For salary, research market data for role, location, and level, then anchor above your target.
- Negotiate the total package (base, bonus, equity, start date), and ask for time before accepting.
- Send a follow-up within 24 hours referencing one specific point from the conversation.
- For career changes, map transferable strengths to the target role's requirements and close gaps with one concrete project or certification.

title: Travel Planning
hint: Trip itineraries, logistics, seasons, budgets, visas, transport
text:
- Confirm dates, travelers, budget, and pace first; three cities in seven days needs very different logistics than a slow trip.
- Check entry rules early (passport validity, visa or eTA, transit documents) on official government sites.
- Account for seasons: monsoon, hurricane, ski, school-holiday, and festival periods change prices, closures, and crowds.
- Build day-by-day plans with realistic transit times and 30-60 minute buffers between transfers.
- Group activities by geography, and book timed-entry attractions and popular restaurants in advance.
- Estimate costs by category (flights, lodging, transport, food, activities) plus 10-15% contingency, and state currency and price date.
- Mention travel insurance and cancellation terms, plus time zone and the local emergency number.
- Flag that hours, fares, and routes change; verify before booking.

title: Cooking and Recipes
hint: Recipes, quantities, cooking times, substitutions, scaling portions
text:
- Give quantities in grams and milliliters; flour by volume can vary 20% or more.
- State yield, prep time, cook time, and resting time at the top of every recipe.
- Give oven temperatures in C and F, and note the fan-oven adjustment, typically 15-20C lower.
- Specify doneness cues and internal temperatures: poultry 74C (165F), pork 63C with rest, bread around 93-99C inside.
- For substitutions, preserve function: acid for acid, fat for fat, and keep leavening ratios; say when texture will change.
- Scale carefully: salt, spices, and leavening do not scale linearly, and very large batches need longer cooking.
- Warn about common mistakes: overcrowding the pan, salting too late, underseasoning starches, opening the oven too early.
- Include food safety: refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours, and avoid raw egg for pregnant or immunocompromised people.

title: Fitness and Nutrition
hint: Training programs, exercise form, protein intake, calorie targets, weight goals
text:
- Program resistance training around progressive overload: add reps, load, or sets gradually and log them weekly.
- Plan 2-4 weekly sessions, with roughly 10-20 hard sets per muscle group per week for hypertrophy.
- Set protein at about 1.4-2.0 g/kg bodyweight per day for most exercisers; 2.3-3.1 g/kg may help retain lean mass while cutting.
- Spread protein across 3-4 meals of roughly 20-40 g each, or 0.25 g/kg per meal, per the ISSN position stand.
- For fat loss, use a moderate deficit of about 300-500 kcal/day (roughly 0.5-1% of bodyweight per week).
- Include warm-up, technique cues, and 2-3 minute rests for heavy compound lifts.
- Screen before advising intense training: chest pain, dizziness, joint injury, or pregnancy need a clinician first.
- Avoid detox products and extreme diets; creatine monohydrate and caffeine have the strongest supplement evidence.

title: Spreadsheets and Formulas
hint: Excel or Google Sheets formulas, lookups, pivots, data cleanup
text:
- Confirm the app and version first; XLOOKUP and dynamic arrays need current versions, while older Excel lacks them.
- Prefer INDEX/MATCH for compatibility and left-side lookups; XLOOKUP reads well for exact matches with a not-found argument.
- Always use exact match (0 or FALSE) in lookups; approximate match on unsorted data fails silently.
- Use absolute references ($A$1) and bounded ranges; avoid whole-column references in heavy formulas.
- Clean data before formulas: check numbers stored as text, trailing spaces, and mixed date formats; TRIM, VALUE, and DATEVALUE help.
- Wrap lookups in IFNA or IFERROR only where a blank is meaningful, so real errors stay visible.
- Use FILTER, SORT, and UNIQUE for dynamic lists, and check for blocked cells that stop spill ranges.
- Verify with a small known sample and a total check, and record assumptions in a notes tab.

title: Machine Learning Engineering
hint: Model training, evaluation, overfitting, data leakage, metric choice
text:
- Split data before any preprocessing; fit scalers, encoders, and imputers on training data only.
- For time series, use time-based or expanding-window validation and never build features from future rows.
- Split by entity (customer, patient, session) when samples are correlated, so one entity never appears in both train and test.
- Establish a baseline first (majority class, linear model, or last value) and report every experiment against it.
- Diagnose overfitting from train versus validation curves; fix with early stopping, regularization, or simpler models.
- Match metrics to cost: precision and recall for imbalanced classes, PR-AUC when positives are rare, calibration when thresholds matter.
- Treat near-perfect scores as leakage until proven otherwise; ablate suspicious columns.
- Keep the test set untouched until final evaluation; report variance across seeds or folds.

title: Research and Literature Review
hint: Literature reviews, source quality, citation verification, evidence synthesis
text:
- Define the question with PICO (population, intervention, comparison, outcome) or an equivalent before searching.
- Search at least two databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar) and log queries and dates.
- Rank evidence by design: systematic reviews and RCTs above cohort and case-control studies, which rank above expert opinion and blogs.
- Appraise each study with a tool such as the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool or CASP; PRISMA 2020 governs reporting, not study quality.
- Verify every citation by resolving its DOI or PubMed ID; never invent authors, years, volumes, or quotes.
- Check retraction status; separate preprints and predatory journals from peer review.
- Report effect sizes with confidence intervals, not only p-values, and note sample size and heterogeneity.
- State limitations openly; synthesize by theme, not paper by paper.

title: Telegram Bot Development
hint: Building Telegram bots with aiogram or python-telegram-bot
text:
- Organize handlers in Router modules per feature and include them in one Dispatcher; do not attach handlers at module scope.
- Pass shared dependencies (DB session, config) through middleware, not globals.
- Use FSM only for multi-step dialogs; keep state in Redis or a database in production, since in-memory storage is lost on restart.
- Always answer callback queries with callback.answer() to stop the loading spinner.
- Run polling or webhook, never both; verify the webhook secret token and offload heavy work to tasks.
- Respect rate limits (about 30 messages per second overall, 20 per minute per group) and back off on TelegramRetryAfter.
- Make handlers idempotent; record processed update_id values when side effects matter.
- Keep tokens in environment variables and log exceptions with update context via an error handler.
